description: Close documented limitation #3 (SCRIPTING.md line ~131: 'Scripts can't define new mob types, UI screens or rendering. Those need a Rust change.'). Deliver a DATA/SCRIPT path for defining NEW mob types from a mod. This is the large, open-ended feature; scope it to a minimal, well-tested, extensible FIRST VERSION of mob definitions, and explicitly document the UI-screen and custom-rendering sub-scope as deferred with concrete blockers if they can't be done cleanly here. Design constraint from exploration: mobs are a hardcoded `enum MobKind` in src/entity.rs with a fixed 33-entry ALL array; index()/from_index() produce a u8 used over the wire (src/net.rs MobSnap.kind, src/multiplayer.rs snapshots) and from_name() maps strings (used by scripting spawn_mob and the mod `spawn` action). Approach: introduce a registry of mod-defined mob definitions and a `MobKind::Modded(u16)` variant (or an equivalent id-based representation) that indexes it, with every `match self` dispatch in entity.rs gaining a Modded arm that reads the def. Mob defs are declared in mod.txt via a new `[mob <name>]` section (data, so they sync to joined clients exactly like blocks/items, keeping multiplayer host-authoritative and deterministic); the existing scripting `spawn_mob(name, x, y, z)` and the mod `spawn <name>` action then resolve mod mob names for free. Persisted/wire mob kind must stay save-compatible: store mod mobs BY NAME in saves and degrade gracefully (unknown mob kind on load -> drop the mob, like removed-mod blocks become air); over the wire, the index is valid because the host's mods are sent to clients so both build the same deterministic registry order.
steps: DEEP READ before coding: src/entity.rs MobKind (enum ~165, ALL ~227, index/from_index/from_name/name ~263, dims ~155-ish within impl, max_health, hostile ~427, burns/fireproof/flies, loot ~1371, extra_loot ~1410, draw ~1444, model() dispatch ~1927, the `Part` static templates like OINKER/GROANER and the `part(...)`/draw_posed helpers), the Mob struct (~467) and how `kind` is stored/spawned; src/net.rs MobSnap (~53, ~856) and how kind:u8 is written/read; src/multiplayer.rs mob snapshot encode (~1256) and decode (~1102, from_index); src/mods.rs section parsing (how [block]/[item] sections are discovered and allotted ids in a first pass, then filled -- replicate that two-pass id-allotment pattern for [mob]); src/block.rs Registry struct (add a mobs field) and ModArmor/ItemDef as the pattern for a new ModMob struct; src/scripting.rs spawn_mob (~237) and block_exists; how `spawn` mod-action resolves mob names (search for from_name usages). Write down every match-on-MobKind site that needs a Modded arm.

DATA MODEL: add a `ModMob` struct (in block.rs next to ModArmor, or entity.rs) holding at minimum: name (display), key (modns:name for save/wire resolution), half_width, height (dims), max_health, speed multiplier, hostile flag, a drop (item id + max count) optional, a texture tile for the body, and a `template` selecting which base-game `Part` model to render with (an enum/index over a curated set like Oinker/Groaner/Bloop/Cluckster so the first version reuses existing geometry with the mod's texture tint/tile). Add `pub mobs: Vec<ModMob>` to Registry and initialize it empty in Registry::base() and in the install path. Keep it clamped/bounded like other mod data (sane caps on dims/health/speed; cap mob count).

MOBKIND INTEGRATION: add `MobKind::Modded(u16)` (index into reg().mobs). Update MobKind::ALL handling and index()/from_index() so base-game kinds keep their existing stable indices (append-only) and modded kinds occupy indices after the base set in deterministic registry order (so host and clients agree because they share mods). Update from_name() to fall back to reg().mobs lookup by key when the base match misses. Update name(), dims(), max_health(), hostile(), burns()/fireproof()/flies() (and any other `match self` that must be total) with a Modded arm pulling from the def, choosing safe defaults for behaviors not in the data model (e.g. modded mobs are passive wanderers reusing an existing simple AI/animation path; do NOT give them special boss/raid/tameable behavior in v1). Update loot()/extra_loot() Modded arm to use the def's drop. Update model() and draw() so a Modded mob renders with its template's Part slice and its texture tile. Ensure the AI tick path handles Modded without panicking (reuse a passive-wander branch).

SPAWNING + AUTHORITY: ensure spawn_mob(name,...) in scripting.rs and the mod `spawn <name>` action resolve a mod mob name through from_name() and spawn it host-side only (same path as base mobs), so it is host-authoritative and replicated via the normal snapshot. Confirm mobs_near and on_mob_death still work; on_mob_death passes a kind name string -- make sure a modded mob reports its key/name. Do NOT let joined clients author mobs.

SERIALIZATION / SAVE-COMPAT: over the wire, keep MobSnap.kind as the registry index (deterministic across host+clients since mods are synced); verify from_index(idx) resolves modded kinds. For SAVES (src/save.rs and wherever mobs persist, if they do -- check whether mobs are saved at all or only regenerated; many of these games don't persist loose mobs, so confirm), if mobs are persisted, store the mod mob BY NAME/key (not raw index) and on load resolve by name; if the key is unknown (mod removed/renamed), drop that mob gracefully (mirroring 'removed-mod blocks become air'). If mobs are NOT persisted to saves, document that and ensure the wire index path is the only concern. Add an explicit test that a modded mob kind round-trips through the net MobSnap encode/decode (reuse the existing net test pattern around line 1541) and resolves back to the same mod mob.

MOD.TXT PARSING: add `[mob <name>]` to the section list in mods.rs with a two-pass id allotment like blocks/items (first pass registers the name -> index, second pass fills the ModMob fields), parsing keys: name, texture, health, speed, size/width/height, hostile (bool), drops (item + count), template/model (one of the curated base templates). Emit clear `line N: ...` errors for unknown textures/items/templates, consistent with existing mod errors, and keep the rest of the mod loading on error. Enforce the documented caps.

SCRIPTING API (optional, if clean): optionally expose a read-only helper or confirm spawn_mob already covers script-driven spawning of the data-defined mob. The REQUIREMENT is that scripts can cause new mob types to exist and spawn; defining the type via mod.txt data (which the script mod ships alongside its .rhai) satisfies 'scripts can define new mob types' because a code mod is a folder that can contain both. Do NOT attempt a full runtime Rhai mob-definition API in v1 unless it is trivially clean.

UI SCREENS / CUSTOM RENDERING (deferred sub-scope): investigate whether a bounded hook is feasible; if not clean within this feature, DO NOT force it. Instead, in the feature findings and in SCRIPTING.md, clearly document what was delivered (data/script-defined mob TYPES with stats, drops, and a templated render) versus deferred (arbitrary custom UI screens and bespoke per-mob rendering/geometry), with the concrete blockers (e.g. rendering is tied to static `Part` templates and the macroquad draw path; UI screens are driven by Rust state machines in ui.rs/main.rs with no scripting surface). Make a genuine attempt to assess feasibility before deferring.

TESTS: add regression tests: (a) mods.rs parse test: a `[mob <name>]` section produces a ModMob in reg().mobs with the expected fields and from_name(key) resolves to MobKind::Modded(i); (b) entity.rs test: a modded MobKind returns the def's dims/max_health/name/loot and model() returns a non-empty Part slice (no panic across the dispatch); (c) net/multiplayer test: a modded mob kind survives MobSnap encode->decode and from_index round-trip; (d) a graceful-degradation test: from_index/from_name for an out-of-range or unknown mod mob returns None (or drops) rather than panicking. All tests must build under --no-default-features and be clippy-clean.

DOCS + EXAMPLE: update SCRIPTING.md line ~131 to state that mods can now define new mob types (via a [mob] section in mod.txt, spawnable from scripts with spawn_mob), and keep the UI/rendering caveat with the deferred scope spelled out. Add a `[mob <name>]` section + its keys to MODDING.md (a new table consistent with [block]/[item]). Optionally add a demonstrative mob to example-mods/cheese (or a new tiny example) ONLY if it keeps the example-loads-cleanly test green.
Run `cargo test --no-default-features` and `cargo clippy --no-default-features --all-targets`; confirm all pass and zero warnings. Commit onto branch `guh`. Do NOT push.
acceptance_criteria: A mod can declare a new mob type via a `[mob <name>]` section in mod.txt; after loading, reg().mobs contains it and MobKind::from_name(key) resolves to a Modded kind.
spawn_mob(name,...) from a script and the `spawn <name>` mod action spawn the mod-defined mob host-side; it is replicated to clients via the normal snapshot (deterministic, host-authoritative).

Every MobKind dispatch in entity.rs (name/dims/max_health/hostile/loot/model/draw and the AI tick) handles Modded without panicking; the mob renders using a templated Part model and its texture, and drops its defined item.

A modded mob kind round-trips through net MobSnap encode/decode and from_index; an unknown/removed mod mob degrades gracefully (dropped on load / returns None) without scrambling the world or panicking.
SCRIPTING.md and MODDING.md document the new mob-definition capability; the UI-screen/custom-rendering portion is explicitly scoped as delivered-vs-deferred with concrete blockers.
`cargo test --no-default-features` passes with new tests; `cargo clippy --no-default-features --all-targets` is clean; Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock unchanged; base-game mobs behave identically.
verification: Read the new tests and confirm the modded-mob dispatch, spawn, and net round-trip tests would fail if the Modded arms or the registry wiring were removed; confirm graceful-degradation test covers the unknown-kind path.
findings: DELIVERED: data/script path for new mob TYPES. (1) block.rs: added `ModMob` struct {key,name,tile,half_width,height,max_health,speed,hostile,drop,template} and `MobTemplate` enum {Quadruped,Biped,Blob,Bird} with from_name(); added `pub mobs: Vec<ModMob>` to Registry, initialized empty in Registry::base(). (2) entity.rs: added `MobKind::Modded(u16)` variant plus consts BASE_MOBS (=33) and MAX_MOD_MOBS (=222, so index fits a u8 alongside base kinds). index()/from_index() give modded kinds indices BASE_MOBS+i in deterministic registry order; from_index returns None for out-of-range (graceful). from_name() falls back to reg().mobs by full key or bare name. Added mod_def() and script_name() helpers. Every match-on-self dispatch gained a Modded arm (name/dims/max_health/xp_value/hostile; passive/flies/fireproof/burns/raider return false by matches! so modded mobs are safe passive wanderers; breed_food []), loot() reads the def's drop, the AI tick's big match + damage() got Modded arms (flee when hit, else wander), model() returns an OINKER fallback and a new `modded_parts(def)` builds runtime Parts from a base template re-textured with the mod tile; draw() special-cases Modded to use modded_parts. game.rs: two exhaustiveness arms (idle chatter, death advancements) + on_mob_death now uses script_name(). (3) mods.rs: `[mob <name>]` parsed with the same two-pass id-allotment as [block]/[item] (pass 1 reserves the ModMob slot by key in deterministic order, pass 2 fill_mob fills texture/template/size/width/height/health/speed/hostile/drops with clamps + clear line-N errors). The mod `spawn <name>` action resolves via a new Ctx::spawn_kind that looks at the registry being built (not the installed one) via MobKind::from_base_name_public, so a mod can spawn its own mob from an item action. (4) SPAWN/AUTHORITY: scripting spawn_mob and the spawn action produce Cmd::Spawn/Action::Spawn(index) which game.rs resolves host-side with from_index and alloc_mob; Action::Spawn already refuses on clients ('Only the host can spawn mobs'). (5) WIRE: MobSnap.kind stays the u8 registry index; deterministic because mods sync to clients. multiplayer sync_mobs uses from_index which now resolves modded kinds. (6) SAVE: mobs ARE persisted (animals::encode_mobs for tamed/bred/fed/named mobs only). Modded mobs are now stored BY NAME: a 255 sentinel kind byte + length-prefixed modid:name key; decode_mobs_named resolves by name and DROPS the record (consuming its bytes, continue) if the mod is gone -- mirrors removed-mod blocks becoming air. Base kinds never reach 255 (capped by MAX_MOD_MOBS). TESTS added (all build under --no-default-features, clippy-clean): mods::tests::mods_define_new_mob_types, a_mob_section_needs_a_name, mod_mob_resolves_by_name_once_installed; entity::tests::base_mob_indices_round_trip, modded_mob_dispatch_is_total_and_wanders_without_panicking; net::tests::a_modded_mob_kind_survives_the_wire; animals::tests::modded_mobs_save_by_name_and_degrade_gracefully. New tests that touch the global registry take crate::mods::registry_test_lock()/with_mods(). Test count 243 -> 250, clippy 0 warnings. DOCS: SCRIPTING.md line ~131 rewritten (mob types now definable + spawnable from scripts; UI/rendering explicitly deferred); MODDING.md gained a `[mob <name>]` schema table, a spawn_mob example, updated Limits (222 mod mobs) and the save/multiplayer note (mod mobs saved by name, dropped if mod removed). EXAMPLE: example-mods/cheese gained a `[mob cheese_mouse]` and its Summoning Brie now spawns it; the_shipped_example_mod_loads_cleanly stays green (mob adds don't change the (5,4,7) added counts). DEFERRED (concrete blockers, genuine feasibility assessment): (a) bespoke per-mob geometry -- rendering is tied to static `Part` template slices and the macroquad draw_posed path; v1 reuses a curated base template re-textured, which is the clean bounded hook. Arbitrary geometry would need a data model for Parts + validation + a new draw path. (b) custom UI screens -- game screens are Rust state machines in ui.rs/main.rs with no scripting surface or registry hook; adding one safely is a separate, larger Rust change. (c) code behaviours (bosses/taming/trading/flying/custom attacks) deliberately out of scope so no data-defined mob can wedge the AI; modded mobs are passive wanderers. CONSTRAINTS MET: additive only; base-game mobs behave identically (base match arms unchanged); host-authoritative + deterministic; save-compatible by name with graceful degradation; Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock untouched.
